message.content:
Below is a quick‑look table of the **federal long‑weekend holidays** in Canada for 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the “observed” day is the following Monday, which still creates a 3‑day weekend.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if applicable) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Monday Jan 2 | Sat Jan 1 – Mon Jan 3 |
| Family Day (BC, AB, SK, MB, ON, NB, PE) | Monday Feb 20 | — | Sat Feb 18 – Mon Feb 20 |
| Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | — | Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9 |
| Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | — | Sat May 20 – Mon May 22 |
| Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | Monday Jul 3 | Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3 |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | — | Sat Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4 |
| Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | — | Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9 |
| Remembrance Day | Monday Nov 11 | — | Sat Nov 9 – Mon Nov 11 |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | — | Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25 |

> **Note:**  
> • Boxing Day (Dec 26) falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does **not** create a long weekend.  
> • Some provinces have additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. John’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, etc.) that can also produce long weekends, but the table above lists the federal holidays that apply nationwide.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app or let me know if you’d like province‑specific long‑weekends added!
